title: CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) message
summary: CoAP is a lightweight REST protocol for constrained IoT devices (RFC 7252). Messages are carried over UDP. Header: version (2 bits), type (2 bits: confirmable, non-confirmable, acknowledgment, reset), token length (4 bits), code (1 byte: class.method), message ID (2 bytes). Then token, options (TLV), payload (preceded by 0xFF marker).

structure.meaning: Class (3 bits) . Method (5 bits): 0.00 empty, 0.01 GET, 0.02 POST, 0.03 PUT, 0.04 DELETE, 2.xx success, 4.xx client error, 5.xx server error.
Message identifier for matching requests to responses.
Token for matching requests to responses (independent of message ID).
TLV options: delta-encoded option number, length, value. Options: Uri-Host, Uri-Port, Uri-Path, Uri-Query, Content-Format, Accept, ... .
The message body (e.g., JSON, CBOR, or raw bytes).

ext.example_decoded: CoAP CON GET request: version 1, type 0 (CON), token length 0, code 0.01 (GET), message ID 1
notes: CoAP uses UDP (default port 5683, 5684 for DTLS).
Confirmable messages require an ACK; non-confirmable do not.
Observe option (RFC 7641) enables pub/sub for resource changes.
Block-wise transfer (RFC 7959) splits large payloads into smaller blocks.
CoAP can be proxied to HTTP and vice versa (RFC 8075).
